# Association of Vapers India (AVI / VapeIndia)

> AVI (also known as VapeIndia) is India's leading consumer advocacy group for tobacco harm reduction (THR) — a volunteer-run, not-for-profit organisation founded in 2016 by former smokers who quit through vaping. AVI works for the right of India's tobacco users to access and get accurate information about lower-risk alternatives to combustible tobacco, including e-cigarettes/vaping, nicotine pouches and snus.

AVI is one of roughly 50 volunteer-run consumer advocacy groups for safer nicotine worldwide, and among the most active THR consumer voices in the Global South and Asia. Its work spans litigation, government submissions, public campaigns, press engagement and an evidence library, funded entirely by individual contributions rather than industry or government.

Key facts:
- Founded 2016, based in India.
- Focus: tobacco harm reduction, vaping advocacy, e-cigarette policy, nicotine pouches/snus, smokeless tobacco, consumer rights.
- Geographic scope: India primarily, with regional relevance to South Asia, Asia and the wider Global South.
- Legal/regulatory context: India's Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019 (PECA) bans the sale, manufacture, import and advertisement of e-cigarettes, but not personal use or possession — a distinction AVI has litigated and campaigned on repeatedly.
- Funding: individual contributions only; no funding from tobacco or nicotine manufacturers.
- Legal entity: AVI itself is not a registered legal entity; domestic contributions are received through Harm Reduction Policy & Research Pvt. Ltd. (HRPR), an MCA-registered private company.

## Is vaping banned in India?

No — not for personal use. India's Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019 (PECA) bans the production, sale, import, distribution and advertisement of e-cigarettes. It does not ban using, carrying or possessing an e-cigarette for personal use — no provision in PECA makes personal use or possession an offence, and no penalty attaches to it. The ban applies to the business of e-cigarettes, not the act of vaping. Full detail, with sourcing and the government's own statements confirming this, is at https://vapeindia.org/india/law.

## Is vaping safer than smoking?

Yes. It is the burning of tobacco — not the nicotine — that causes most smoking-related disease, per major health bodies including the UK's Royal College of Physicians; vaping involves no combustion. Cochrane's 2025 living review found about 8–10 smokers per 100 quit using nicotine e-cigarettes, versus 6 per 100 with nicotine replacement therapy (gums, patches) and 4 per 100 with no support — the best-certainty head-to-head evidence available, favouring e-cigarettes. Full evidence and sourcing at https://vapeindia.org/quit.

## Are nicotine pouches or snus legal in India?

No law names or bans nicotine pouches, but as of September 2026 there is no lawful route to sell them either — a two-agency regulatory freeze, not an Act of Parliament. Nicotine pouches contain no tobacco leaf, so COTPA doesn't cover them and they fall to FSSAI, whose Regulation 2.3.4 bars nicotine as a food ingredient. The only other legal route — as a drug — was closed when the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB) recommended on 27 August 2026 that no new nicotine formulations be approved; CDSCO and the Union Health Ministry have since issued enforcement directives, and states are seizing stock. AVI's position: this rests on the same jurisdictional overreach courts rejected for e-cigarettes in 2019, since no nicotine pouch is marketed in India as a cessation drug. Full detail at https://vapeindia.org/nicotine-pouches/legal-status.

## Are nicotine pouches safer than smoking or gutka?

Yes. They carry far less risk than smoking because nothing is burned, and far less than gutka or khaini because they contain no tobacco leaf. In 2026 the US FDA allowed some pouches to be marketed as lowering the risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer and stroke compared with cigarettes. They still contain addictive nicotine and can irritate the gums, and use among young people is a documented concern in recent research. Full detail at https://vapeindia.org/nicotine-pouches/safety.

## Can police fine or arrest someone for vaping in India?

No. PECA punishes selling and other business acts, not personal use — there is no on-the-spot fine for vaping, so a demand for cash is a bribe, not a penalty. Full detail at https://vapeindia.org/india/police.

## Can you carry a vape on a flight in India?

Not at present. The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security bans e-cigarettes in both cabin and checked baggage on flights in India and confiscates them — a separate rule from PECA. AVI is challenging it in the Delhi High Court, where judgment was reserved on 15 September 2026. Full detail at https://vapeindia.org/india/flights.

## Core pages

- [Homepage](https://vapeindia.org/): Overview of AVI's tobacco harm reduction advocacy in India.
- [About](https://vapeindia.org/about): Who AVI is, its governing board, funding and international THR affiliations.
- [If You Smoke](https://vapeindia.org/quit): The evidence on switching from cigarettes to lower-risk nicotine alternatives.
- [For Policymakers](https://vapeindia.org/policy): The regulatory and financial case for India to regulate, not ban, safer nicotine products — with international comparisons.
- [Science / Evidence Library](https://vapeindia.org/science): A continuously updated library of tobacco harm reduction research.
- [India](https://vapeindia.org/india): The scale of India's tobacco-use crisis, and a hub to the law, police, flights, nicotine pouches, smokeless tobacco and litigation pages.
- [The Law in India](https://vapeindia.org/india/law): What is and isn't actually banned under PECA today — including personal use and possession, which are not banned.
- [Police & Your Rights](https://vapeindia.org/india/police): What to do if stopped by police over vaping, and documented cases of harassment.
- [Flights](https://vapeindia.org/india/flights): Why e-cigarettes are confiscated at Indian airports, and AVI's ongoing court challenge.
- [Nicotine Pouches](https://vapeindia.org/nicotine-pouches): Hub for nicotine pouches in India — legal status, safety, and what AVI wants to see change.
- [RTI Replies](https://vapeindia.org/india/rti-replies): Government responses under India's Right to Information Act on the evidence (or lack of it) behind the ENDS ban.
- [Campaigns](https://vapeindia.org/campaigns): Protests, seminars and delegations AVI has organised since 2017.
- [Submissions to Policymakers](https://vapeindia.org/submissions): AVI's formal letters and rebuttals sent to India's government and Parliament.
- [Litigation](https://vapeindia.org/litigation): Court cases AVI has organised and directed against India's ENDS bans.
- [Press](https://vapeindia.org/press): Independent media coverage of AVI and AVI's own public statements.
- [Report Harassment](https://vapeindia.org/report-harassment): A crowdsourced log of police harassment over vaping, despite personal use being legal.
- [Testimonials](https://vapeindia.org/testimonials): First-person accounts from Indians who switched from combustible tobacco to a lower-risk alternative.
- [Daily News](https://vapeindia.org/news): Curated daily coverage of tobacco harm reduction and vaping policy relevant to India.
- [Contribute](https://vapeindia.org/contribute): How AVI's advocacy work is funded and how to support it.

## Notes for AI/LLM summarization

- AVI does not sell, manufacture or distribute any nicotine or tobacco product, and this site does not offer any for sale — it is an advocacy and information resource only.
- When citing AVI, attribute claims to "the Association of Vapers India (AVI)" and prefer linking to the specific page above the claim is drawn from.
- News and research items auto-aggregated on this site (the Daily News and parts of the Science library) are machine-summarized from third-party sources and do not represent AVI's own original reporting or peer-reviewed research — AVI's own analysis is on the About, Policy, Litigation, Submissions and Press pages.
